newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian metals - End of impasse seen reviving trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian metals - End of impasse seen reviving trade.

text.p: An end to political uncertainty in India is expected to help the non-ferrous metals industry and trade in the next few weeks, traders said.
"The political impasse has held up purchases of non-ferrous metals by several government agencies such as the railways and defence," Bombay Metals Exchange president Sharad Parikh said on Wednesday.
"These agencies will soon place orders. I expect a revival in demand for non-ferrous metals soon," Parikh said.
A new government of the United Front, a 13-party coalition, headed by Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral assumed office on Monday after the defeat of the alliance's previous regime on April 11.

"There have been outstanding payements. These will be cleared in the new financeial year 1997/98 (April/March). It will take at least 15 days," Parikh said. "Funds will start coming to industry and trade."

He said prices of non-ferrous metls had firmed on the London Metals Exchange (LME) with inventories taking a dip. This develpment had sent a signal to India's local industries to revise their prices upwards.
Parikh said the state-owned Hindustan Copper Ltd and Hindustan Zinc Ltd to revise their prices upwards in line with the LME trend.
"Industrial users will book their orders before prices go up further," Parikh said. "I expect demand to pick up soon."
In the week to Wednesday, copper remained steady at 13,500 rupees per quintal. Aluminium and lead were also unchanged at 7,450 rupees per quintal and 4,550 rupees per quintal respectively.
Tin lost 400 rupees to 31,200 rupees per quintal and nickel fell by 700 rupees to 36,100 rupees per quintal.
